title: Lyra - embeddings & rerank discovery
next_steps: Send hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet
Run 1-week benchmark with 100k vectors + rerank pipeline
Schedule POC scoping call for week of 2025-10-06
action_items: Maya: send pricing and example pricing calc by 2025-10-04
Jonah: draft benchmark plan and required data format by 2025-10-03
James: share current embed pipeline and sample vectors (CSV/NDJSON) by 2025-10-03
summary: Discovery call to understand Lyra's use of embeddings/reranking, vector DB integrations, throughput requirements, and build vs managed tradeoffs. Main concerns: tail latency for rerank, vector dimensionality, hybrid search (ann + lexical), security/SAML, and whether to run Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
topics: vector DB choice and hybrid search
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, our AE, with Jonah our SE. quick introductions?
[00:08] Sarah Kim: Hi, Sarah here, CTO at Lyra Analytics, James and Rajesh are on from engineering.
[00:12] James Park: Hey, James.
[00:14] Rajesh Gupta: Rajesh, infra.
[00:16] Jonah Rivera: Great, thanks. The aim today is to understand embeddings use, reranking flow, and where Redwood might fit—hosted, dedicated, or private.
[00:24] Lina Torres: We're evaluating options for document search + a rerank stage, want to reduce false positives and improve relevance for enterprise customers.
[00:30] Jonah Rivera: Nice. Can you walk through your current pipeline?
[00:34] James Park: Sure. Right now we use OpenAI text-embedding-3-small to generate 1536-d vectors, store in Pinecone. Retrieval is ANN for top-200, then a transformer-based cross-encoder for rerank. Latency is okay for batch but p95 during peak spikes hits 700-900ms which makes UX rough.
[00:53] Maya Patel: That's helpful. When you say peak spikes, what's QPS and vector size?
[00:57] James Park: Typical QPS to search is ~15-25, burst to 80-100 for some customers. Index size about 1.2M vectors.
[01:05] Rajesh Gupta: Important to note we have strict data residency needs—some customers require EU-only, and we need SAML SSO. Also audit logs are a must.
[01:14] Jonah Rivera: Understood. On the model side, are you open to using different embedding dims or models? 1536 is common but lower dims could reduce storage/ANN cost.
[01:23] James Park: We experimented with 768 dim models, but went back to 1536 because rerank quality improved. But if the candidate set quality is better we could consider lower dims + richer reranker.
[01:32] Maya Patel: Have you tried hybrid search—ANN plus lexical BM25 for recency or keyword precision?
[01:36] James Park: We do a simple filter by metadata, but haven't fully implemented hybrid ranking. Would like to.
[01:41] Lina Torres: The product asks for hybrid because sometimes named entities and exact matches are crucial.
[01:46] Jonah Rivera: Redwood supports hybrid approaches—our retrieval layer can combine vector distance with lexical signals and we expose rerank hooks. For Dedicated/Private you can colocate embedding pipelines to reduce token transit.
[01:56] Sarah Kim: How does Redwood handle throughput? If we move to Dedicated, what's the typical per-GPU QPS for embedding lookup + rerank?
[02:03] Jonah Rivera: It varies by model and GPU. For vector search we optimize the ANN index per-shard; on Dedicated a single worker can serve thousands of small queries if you use batching and optimized kernels. For rerank cross-encoder inference we recommend separate worker pools—GPU instances can do ~100-300 cross-encoder reranks per second depending on model size and batch config.
[02:22] Rajesh Gupta: That 100-300/sec, is that for a 6-layer cross-encoder or full BERT-large? We use a medium-sized cross-encoder, maybe ~110M params.
[02:30] Jonah Rivera: For medium cross-encoder, 100-200 QPS is realistic per GPU with optimized batching. If you need lower tail latency we do model distillation or shard rerank across smaller CPUs—there are tradeoffs.
[02:42] James Park: For us p95 of 700ms is mostly the cross-encoder stage. If we can move rerank to sub-300ms p95 that'd be a big win.
[02:49] Maya Patel: Sounds like a POC to benchmark end-to-end is the right next step. We'll need sample data and expected SLAs.
[02:55] Sarah Kim: Agreed. One question: how tightly coupled is Redwood to specific vector DBs? We currently run Pinecone but are open to switching.
[03:04] Jonah Rivera: Redwood can integrate with managed vector DBs (Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate) or you can use our hosted index service. For Dedicated/Private you can bring your own DB in VPC or use Redwood's indexing layer. There's also an option to pin embeddings to objects for cheaper storage.
[03:20] Rajesh Gupta: On the security front, do you support customer-managed KMS and HSM for keys?
[03:24] Maya Patel: Yes, for Private deployments we integrate with KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), and Dedicated can be configured for CMK policies. We also have audit logs and RBAC.
[03:33] Sarah Kim: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO certificates we can share?
[03:36] Maya Patel: Yes, we will share the compliance pack—SOC 2 Type II, and our ISO docs. We'll include required attestation.
[03:42] James Park: On the embedding side—do you recommend producing embeddings in Redwood or do we keep generating client-side and push to index? Latency-wise what's best?
[03:50] Jonah Rivera: Both patterns are supported. Hosted API is simplest: send text to Redwood, we return embeddings and can forward to your vector DB or hosted index. For Dedicated, colocating embedder next to index reduces network overhead and improves throughput. For Private on-prem, you keep embeddings local. For throughput, client-side generation with batch uploads is cost-effective, but colocated generation lowers end-to-end latency.
[04:11] Lina Torres: If we did a POC, what's the minimal data set you need?
[04:14] Jonah Rivera: For a representative rerank POC, 50k-200k vectors plus a few hundred to a few thousand labeled queries for relevance tests is ideal. You can also start with 10k if you want a quick sanity check.
[04:26] James Park: We have 120k vectors and about 500 annotated queries. We'll prepare a sanitized sample.
[04:31] Maya Patel: Great. Regarding dimensionality and index type—what about quantization? We heard about 8-bit/4-bit quantization but not sure where that fits for embeddings.
[04:39] Jonah Rivera: Quantization is more about model weights for inference; for embeddings you can compress vectors using product quantization (PQ) or OPQ in ANN indexes which reduces storage and speeds up search with some recall loss. Redwood's index configs can run PQ with adjustable codebooks so you can trade recall for storage/throughput.
[04:57] Rajesh Gupta: Important: we need hybrid search so we can't lose recall on named entities. Can we do a fallback to exact lexical match when confidence low?
[05:06] Jonah Rivera: Yes—indexing and query-time rerank can combine lexical filters and exact-match checks. We can set confidence thresholds where lexical match bumps a result. It's configurable.
[05:15] Sarah Kim: Pricing question—what are the cost drivers for hosted vs dedicated?
[05:19] Maya Patel: Hosted is usage-based—per-embedding and per-token for generation. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits; higher upfront but predictable per-QPS costs. Private has licensing + support. We'll send example pricing models.
[05:31] James Park: For benchmarking, what metrics should we capture? p50/p95/p99, throughput, recall@k, MRR, cost per query?
[05:38] Jonah Rivera: Yes to all. Also tokenization time, embedding generation time, index lookup time, rerank time, and end-to-end latency under burst traffic. We'll instrument with traces.
[05:47] Lina Torres: Are there limits on vector dimensionality? We think 1536 is fine but curious if very high dims e.g., 3072 cause issues.
[05:55] Jonah Rivera: Larger dims increase storage and index complexity; some ANN libraries handle it well but throughput drops and memory use increases. We typically recommend staying under 2048, but depends on your accuracy needs. We can test higher dims in POC.
[06:06] Rajesh Gupta: For Private deployment, what's the network topology—do we get a control plane in Redwood cloud and data plane in our VPC?
[06:12] Maya Patel: Exactly—control plane optional: for Private we can provision a customer-managed control plane or a light control plane with the data plane in your VPC. We'll go through specifics in security pack.
[06:21] Sarah Kim: Any gotchas around migration from Pinecone?
[06:24] Jonah Rivera: Data export is straightforward—vector dumps + metadata. We have scripts to reindex into our hosted indexes or connectors to common DBs. For live cutover we recommend a dual-write period.
[06:33] James Park: One more: how do you handle model upgrades and regressions in rerank? We need evals.
[06:38] Jonah Rivera: Redwood Optimize provides eval suites—prompt/eval-driven quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to datasets. You can pin model versions and run A/B rollouts for rerank models.
[06:48] Maya Patel: OK wrapping up—recap of next steps?
[06:51] Sarah Kim: We'll share sample vectors and query labels.
[06:54] James Park: Yep, I'll export sanitized samples.
[06:56] Maya Patel: We'll send pricing and security pack and a benchmark plan from Jonah.
[07:01] Jonah Rivera: I'll draft benchmark plan and specs for the 1-week run, include required formats (NDJSON, schema).
[07:06] Rajesh Gupta: Let's lock a follow-up POC scoping call for week of 10/6.
[07:10] Maya Patel: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:12] Sarah Kim: Thanks.
[07:13] [END OF TRANSCRIPT]
